title: Restriction coherence and replacement independence for localized Kan-diagram evaluation
statement:
Use simplicial sets and coherent functor quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent realization adjunction of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and infinity localization of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$, and let all indexing simplicial sets and values be $\mathcal V$-small; form the diagram categories and their localizations in a containing universe. Write $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V})$. For each simplicial set $K$, not necessarily a quasicategory, let $\mathsf D_K^f$ be the ordinary category of enriched functors $\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$ with Kan values and enriched natural maps, and let $W_K$ be its objectwise weak homotopy equivalences. Put $\mathcal L_K=N(\mathsf D_K^f)[W_K^{-1}]_\infty$ with localization map $q_K$. Let $e_K:N(\mathsf D_K^f)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ be enriched evaluation $e_K(P)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P)\eta_K$, and let $E_K:\mathcal L_K\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ be its localized comparison, with $E_Kq_K\simeq e_K$, as specified in [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation].

For every simplicial map $v:K'\to K$, ordinary restriction $v^*P=P\mathfrak C[v]$ preserves $W_K$ and objectwise Kan diagrams, and induces $\overline{v^*}:\mathcal L_K\to\mathcal L_{K'}$. The exact evaluation identity $e_{K'}(v^*P)=e_K(P)v$ induces a coherent natural equivalence $E_{K'}\overline{v^*}\simeq v^*E_K$. These comparisons are jointly coherent for identity maps, composites of indexing maps, ordinary diagram transformations and all higher simplices of their infinity localizations.

For every ordinary functorial projective cofibrant replacement $Q_K$ on $\mathsf D_K^f$ with its natural trivial fibration $a_K:Q_K\to1$, the maps $e_K(a_K)$ are natural equivalences, and their induced comparisons through $E_Kq_K\simeq e_K$ are coherently compatible with restriction and independent of the replacement. In particular, comparison after restriction uses $Q_{K'}(v^*P)\to v^*P$, without requiring $v^*(Q_KP)$ to be projectively cofibrant. No simplicial enrichment of $Q_K$ is assumed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.2.4.4 and the entire-functor-category universal property of infinity localization: agent-formulated restriction coherence and replacement independence extracted from universal-family old step 6. No Stacks tag. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: For a vertex $x$ of $K'$, $(v^*P)(x)=P(vx)$, and $(v^*a)_x=a_{vx}$. Thus restriction preserves Kan values and objectwise weak equivalences. Functoriality of $\mathfrak C$ gives $1^*=1$ and $(vw)^*=w^*v^*$, including their action on enriched natural maps. Apply the localization universal property of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to $q_{K'}N(v^*)$, which inverts $W_K$. It gives $\overline{v^*}:\mathcal L_K\to\mathcal L_{K'}$ with $\overline{v^*}q_K\simeq q_{K'}N(v^*)$. We use the whole functor-category universal property here, not a statement only about homotopy categories.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4; agent deduction from its enriched-evaluation comparison and the whole-functor-category localization universal property. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: The evaluation formula in [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation] applies to an arbitrary chain $P_0\to\cdots\to P_n$, encoded by $\widetilde P:\mathfrak C[K]\times[n]\to\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$. Restriction encodes it by $\widetilde P(\mathfrak C[v]\times1)$. Naturality of the unit of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] says $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathfrak C[v])\eta_{K'}=\eta_Kv$. Substitution in that evaluation formula gives equality of the maps $K'\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ before and after evaluation. Hence $e_{K'}N(v^*)=v^*e_K$ as simplicial maps on the entire ordinary nerve. The equality commutes with every simplex operator because both formulas precompose by $1\times\Delta(\alpha)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4; agent deduction from its enriched-evaluation comparison and the whole-functor-category localization universal property. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Here is a simultaneous descent of these equalities, so that the comparisons are coherent rather than separately chosen for each $v$. Put $A_K=(N(\mathsf D_K^f),W_K)$ and $F_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. The classes $W_K$ are systems: identities and composites are objectwise weak equivalences, and homotopies in an ordinary nerve identify the same arrow. By [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation], $e_K$ inverts $W_K$. Thus Step 2 is a natural transformation from the contravariant diagram $A$ to $GF$, in the notation of [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Apply that node's localization functor $L$ and then the counit $LGF\simeq F$ (the right adjoint $G$ is fully faithful). This gives a natural transformation $LA\to F$ whose component restricts to $e_K$ by unit naturality. Its components are the $E_K$ of the item by the localized-evaluation node. For any already specified representatives of $\mathcal L_K,E_K$ and their comparisons to $e_K$, the entire functor-category equivalence transports this construction with those comparisons retained. The restriction of $E_{K'}\overline{v^*}\simeq v^*E_K$ along $q_K$ is precisely the equality of Step 2, conjugated by $E_Jq_J\simeq e_J$.

source.place: Construction 4.1.7.1, Proposition 4.1.7.2 and Notation 4.1.7.3; functorial localization and its natural unit, applied to the strict evaluation transformation.

proof.text: The natural transformation just constructed includes its identity, composition and all iterated composition coherences, since it was obtained by applying a functor and its counit to one diagram. To see why this also retains the diagram variables, write $q_K^*:\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L_K,T)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{W_K}(N(\mathsf D_K^f),T)$ for the equivalence in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Both sides retain all transformations and higher simplices. For any parameter simplicial set $B$, applying $\operatorname{Fun}(B,-)$ to a quasi-inverse and its two natural equivalences gives a quasi-inverse of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,q_K^*)$. Consequently a coherent diagram of comparisons, together with its specified restriction, descends as a whole. Apply this with $B=\Delta^n$ and their boundary and face maps. On the unlocalized side the identity/composite equations are the strict equations in Steps 1--2; their simultaneous descent supplies the same equations with coherent homotopies at every level. The localized functors themselves act on every simplex of $\mathcal L_K$. Thus the comparison is natural on all localized transformations, not just the original ordinary arrows.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7.2 and the entire-functor-category universal property; explicit parameter application of an equivalence and its quasi-inverse.

proof.text: Let $a_K:Q_K\to1$ be the replacement in the statement. Each component is an objectwise weak equivalence between objectwise Kan diagrams, so [lem-coef-kan-diagram-localized-evaluation] makes $e_K(a_{K,P})$ an equivalence. These components form a coherent transformation $b_K=e_KN(a_K):e_KN(Q_K)\to e_K$ since $Q_K,a_K$ are ordinary functorial data. The pointwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], with shape $N(\mathsf D_K^f)$, makes $b_K$ a natural equivalence of entire functors. Moreover $Q_K$ preserves $W_K$: for $f:P\to P'$ the equation $a_{K,P'}Q_K(f)=f a_{K,P}$ and two-out-of-three show $Q_K(f)\in W_K$ whenever $f\in W_K$. The two-out-of-three axiom is part of the model conventions in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Hence $Q_K$ and $a_K$ descend through $q_K$; full faithfulness of its entire functor-category equivalence identifies the descended $b_K$ with its comparison through $E_Kq_K\simeq e_K$. No enriched functor structure on $Q_K$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4; agent deduction from its enriched-evaluation comparison and the whole-functor-category localization universal property. No Stacks tag.

proof.text:
For a restriction $v:K'\to K$, the comparison of replacement evaluations is the zigzag of natural equivalences
$$v^*e_KQ_K\xrightarrow{\ v^*b_K\ }v^*e_K=e_{K'}v^*\xleftarrow{\ b_{K'}v^*\ }e_{K'}Q_{K'}v^*.$$
Thus it uses the fresh replacement $Q_{K'}(v^*P)\to v^*P$ and never asserts cofibrancy of $v^*Q_KP$. Here and below the ordinary nerve on each ordinary functor is suppressed. For two replacements $Q,R$ at the same index, their comparison is $(e_Ka_R)^{-1}(e_Ka_Q)$ in the corresponding functor quasicategory. For three replacements it satisfies
$$((e_Ka_T)^{-1}(e_Ka_R))((e_Ka_R)^{-1}(e_Ka_Q))\simeq(e_Ka_T)^{-1}(e_Ka_Q),$$
using the inverse witnesses and associativity. The same cancellation for $K''\xrightarrow wK'\xrightarrow vK$ cancels $w^*b_{K'}v^*$ and its inverse in the composite restriction comparison, leaving the comparison for $vw$. Identities cancel in the same way. These are compositions of natural equivalences of whole functors, not inverses chosen separately on objects; their inverse witnesses, associativity and higher coherences belong to those functor quasicategories. The whole-functor-category equivalence in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] transports these zigzags and their parameter diagrams to the localizations as in Step 4. This proves joint restriction compatibility and replacement independence, including all higher simplices. Every argument permits empty $K$, empty Kan values, and non-quasicategory shapes; only the containing universe is used for the large diagram categories.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7.2 and whole-functor-category localization; agent-written zigzag and cancellation argument for replacement maps.
